newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia 97/98 asset sales seen at A$9.83 bln.
newsitem.headline: Australia 97/98 asset sales seen at A$9.83 bln.

text.p: The Australian Treasury said on Tuesday it expected asset sales to total A$9.83 billion in 1997/98, implying the proceeds from the sale of one-third of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp would be spread over two years.

The 1997/98 (July-June) estimate, along with an asset sale proceeds estimate of A$5.01 billion for 1998/99, suggested that Telstra may be sold under an instalment payment arrangement, similar to that used for the sale of the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
The specific contribution expected from the Telstra sale was not given, but analysts have said it was likely to raise more than A$8.0 billion.
The government said the sale process was progressing and revealed that it expected all Australian stockbroking firms to be able to sell Telstra shares.

Along with some Telstra proceeds, the government's A$9.83 billion 1997/98 estimate would also include the A$3.34 billion raised through the recent sale of 50-year leases Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports, with the transaction due to be finalised on July 1.
The government expects to sell remaining airports, except for Sydney Airport and the planned Sydney West airport, in the 1997/98 year.
Final instalments were also due from the Commonwealth Bank of Australia sale by November 1997.
The government planned to sell Australian Multimedia Enterprises Ltd by March 1998, although a method of sale was still to be confirmed.
It would also look at sale options, including timing, for Australian Defence Industries Ltd and would offload Auscript as soon as possible by trade sale.
The National Transmission Network, comprising radio transmission equipment and ongoing contracts, would also be considered for sale following the recent completion of a scoping study.
The government would also proceed with plans to sell licences for new radio spectrum as announced in the mid-year review, but an estimated sale proceeds figure was not available.
The sale of Australian National Line Ltd was still anticipated in 1997/98 or the following years.
